text.p: These are the leading stories in the Albanian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The newspaper editorial says a statement by an OSCE diplomat, denying he resigned for personal reasons, has put in doubt Albanians' trust of internatioal democratic institutions monitoring the elections.
- A private aeroplane with four Swiss citizens made an emergency landing outside Tirana. Its passengers were injured.
- An OSCE spokesman denied Albanian election results were being prepared ahead of the vote.
- The new Italian ambassador Marcello Spatafora arrived in Tirana.
- Twelve people were injured when President Sali Berisha's guards exchanged fire with opponents at an election rally in the central town of Elbasan on Thursday.
- Alba multinational troops acknowledge 54 tonnes of lek banknotes arrived at Rinasi airport. The news created fears of inflation.
- 10 people were injured in the central town of Elbasan after clashes as republican guards tried to secure a rally staged by President Sali Berisha.
- A report by the United Nations Development Program says Albania takes the 102nd place in a world list for human development.
- Kamberi company has started to pay back investors.
- Berisha challenges communist terror, the paper says. It is referring to events in Elbasan where at least six people were injured in clashes, including a republican guard officer.
- The Socialist Party should not contest the election outcome, Turkish President Suleyman Demirel is quoted as telling Albanian Prime Minister Bashkim Fino
- Central bank governor Qamil Disha has denied local media allegations that new lek banknotes coming from Malta were printed for political purposes, saying it is about modern and secure notes.
- Paper alleges President Sali Berisha came under fire from Cerrik residents who wanted to revenge attacks his guardsmen launched against their town last month.
- The number of Albanians leaving the country is on the rise.
